newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Rioting Ecuadoran students blow up armored van.
newsitem.headline: Rioting Ecuadoran students blow up armored van.

text.p: Ecuadoran students protesting against the government's austerity program clashed with police and blew up an armored vehicle Friday, police said.
"The anti-riot vehicle was burned, destroyed by dynamite," Col. Jose Teran, chief of the Quito Police Regiment told a local radio station.
No one was hurt in the incident, as the police inside the vehicle got out before the blast.

Police made 54 arrests and two students and seven police were injured in stone-throwing incidents in a third day of protests against a hike of nearly 250 percent in domestic gas prices and more than 100 percent in electricity rates.
The student protests followed a march Wednesday of 5,000 people, led by teachers, through the center of Quito.
Government Minister Frank Vargas asked the students for a truce until President Abdala Bucaram returns from Lima, where he flew for talks with Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori.
Ecuadoran trade unions will fix a date Saturday for a national strike in protest at Bucaram's tough economic reforms, the CMS labor federation said Friday.
Bucaram has said the public services tariff rises result from Congress watering down his tax reforms.
Opposition parties are forming a united front in Congress to fight the tariff rises and block currency convertibility -- the centerpiece of his reforms.
